searchText: its relatively quiet in here and on the rayonism github page, wondering how the efforts towards a testnet are coming along? this is out of sheer curiosity (and excitedness) i appreciate how busy everybody is and isn't meant in any way as criticism Office hour today again, same time as every week. About 5 hours from now <@489217181104734219> the spec is stable, test vectors are there and first clients are passing them, there's just not that much news. We plan to do another devnet next week, maybe more active then. <@!203220829473996800> thank you for responding, but what does that mean for the overall effort of 'the merge'? does it just work out of the box? is there much more to research? to code? Won't be able to join office hour, it's getting late here. Update from us: ran ssz spec tests and discovered an unsupported case in the fssz library. Opened an tracking issue. Working on sharding, block processing is done, epoch processing is next, then networking It is definitely more. First, transition process (a.k.a. docking). We need to figure it out, code and try in test/dev nets. Second, sync algorithms; design work is already happening, then implementation and testing. Block proposal optimisation techniques, communication channel protocol, whether it will be JSON-RPC or REST; user's JSON-RPC modifications (add finalized block method). Writing concrete EIPs that describe execution layer modifications. Solving `BLOCKHASH` randomness problem. Multiple rounds of various kind of testing. Chain tools, get evidence that they work. Infrastructure update, the main question is how block explorers will look like. This is just off the top of my head. If I open the mindmap I can drop more items here. But for now, we focus on Rayonism which is focused on the core of the merge. And then iterate from the results of it. great! I am very happy to hear that you have started your sharding journey test vectors were helpful -- Nimbus passes them fine <@425572898787426305> why is it a main question how explorers will look like? I would have expected this one to be simple: essentially add an execution payload viewer to the current block tab of beaconcha.in, keep eth1 explorers essentially how they are now. So you'd look for blocks in one and transactions in the others <@!755590043632140352> We're working on something like that already (thanks <@!514429265001971732> for getting me started). Running and coupling two explorers is not that easy though. Long-term it may look something like that. Short-term we'll just try to present execution payload contents in a minimal way, to avoid the extra eth1 explorer complexity. But beaconcha.in already links to etherscan, it seems to me that on the long term linking transactions to etherscan or an eth 1 explorer is the way, but in the short term I would have expected to see a link to the execution block We can run two separate explorers, and embed the page of one into the other (or link it), but I'm afraid it will face inconsistencies, delays between indexing the block on one or the other, etc. Long-term I'd like to see the two explorer types integrate more closely Short term I think we can replicate the core functionality directly in the eth2 explorer (And we need to index the basic minimal payload data like the block hash anyway, or else we can't even link to an external explorer) Ok this makes sense to me. Although also beaconcha.in currently does report data in one state and then changes it on the fly when it becomes available: eg attestations are declared missing after some time and then reported when they are seen in a block. This also changes the corresponding links. So something similar seems doable: render the execution payload and then later when it appears in an ex1 explorer link to it Presumably once the branding merges along with the chains, it'll be less viable to communicate with the general Ethereum-using public why a website is a "consensus-layer" browser but not an "execution-layer" browser and vice versa. These are two different use cases, though. An end user should have no interest in what's going on with the consensus side of things. I doubt most eth1 users care deeply about the mempool, but etherscan shows it anyway Quick notes from rayonism office hour call: - Discussed this explorer work (I'm picking it async, prototyping something for next devnet) - Discusssed some sharding block-timing and propagation things - A rough time for next devnet. Setup nodes on Tue, start chain on Wed next week. Regarding the next devnet: - I have more confidence in it now that we have spec tests + previous devnet experience - Mostly the same setup and automation and everything as before, it works - We'll do the mnemonic distribution again, same teams and size. We may even re-use the same keys. If anyone likes to change anything, let me know. More on this next week. - We need a network name. The Rayonism cats painting from earlier name brainstorming was kind of playful, I suggest referencing it in devnet 2. Not sure how to call it though - We'll publish testnet config and genesis data etc. around Monday - The Prysm SSZ bug is the last known interop problem, but there are still many code improvements to make. - The intention of this devnet is to finalize, get a few days, up to a week, of testing done, to prepare for testnet 3. - Just after the end of the hackathon, ~2 weeks from now, I think we should try launch another more public long-running testnet, against which we can work on Eth1 sync tests etc. - Feedback welcome I'd be wary of increasing the requirements for an explorer to be useful. chaind already takes up significant storage just tracking stuff like validator balances and attestation results, so expecting a significant amount of additional data in it will reduce the ability for people to fire it up, obtain data to analyze, etc. <@!203220829473996800> if you use the same keys I don't need to beg Raul again for one 🙂 <@!755590043632140352> haha, you're welcome to get some keys of your own too, I appreciate your debugging help so far Sorry, explorers are rather an _obvious_ example than the _main_ thing of the infra that undergoes changes and is expected to pass through the testing cycle. UI/UX is only a part of the question, the other part is its backend with caveats that Proto has already mentioned. Right, being sure that the block is valid from consensus standpoint is pretty enough for the end user. While staker needs to see other info including transaction fees it got from a block it proposed. sincerely appreciate the thorough response! sorry i was sleeping when you responded you're always welcome! do you think it'd be possible to have the faucet running in the next testnet. I don't expect to have consensus issues, at least we can check this locally before Monday if we interop a few clients and they follow the same chain. I expect that at least Teku, prysm and LH follow the same chain paired with Geth after the transactions issue on prysm is resolved. It would be good to test non-trivial execution payloads in the next testnet. I originally thought that I didn't care about having or not eth, since I can always wait for a block to be produced. But we will not be getting any Tx fees if the blocks are empty 🙂 <@755590043632140352> give me your testnet eth address, and I'll put it into the testnet genesis allocation Right now like this In a couple of hours I'll send it hahaha, nice shot! excerpts.content:
It is definitely more. First, transition process (a.k.a. docking). We need to figure it out, code and try in test/dev nets. Second, sync algorithms; design work is already happening, then implementation and testing. Block proposal optimisation techniques, communication channel protocol, whether it will be JSON-RPC or REST; user's JSON-RPC modifications (add finalized block method). This is just off the top of my head. If I open the mindmap I can drop more items here.

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content:
Quick notes from rayonism office hour call:
- Discussed this explorer work (I'm picking it async, prototyping something for next devnet)
- Discusssed some sharding block-timing and propagation things
- A rough time for next devnet. Setup nodes on Tue, start chain on Wed next week.

Regarding the next devnet:
- I have more confidence in it now that we have spec tests + previous devnet experience
- Mostly the same setup and automation and everything as before, it works
- We'll do the mnemonic distribution again, same teams and size. We may even re-use the same keys. If anyone likes to change anything, let me know. More on this next week.
- We need a network name. The Rayonism cats painting from earlier name brainstorming was kind of playful, I suggest referencing it in devnet 2. Not sure how to call it though
- We'll publish testnet config and genesis data etc. around Monday
- The Prysm SSZ bug is the last known interop problem, but there are still many code improvements to make.
- The intention of this devnet is to finalize, get a few days, up to a week, of testing done, to prepare for testnet 3.
- Just after the end of the hackathon, ~2 weeks from now, I think we should try launch another more public long-running testnet, against which we can work on Eth1 sync tests etc.
- Feedback welcome

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: I'd be wary of increasing the requirements for an explorer to be useful.  chaind already takes up significant storage just tracking stuff like validator balances and attestation results, so expecting a significant amount of additional data in it will reduce the ability for people to fire it up, obtain data to analyze, etc.
